where: Section 1 bullet on DC generator vs Quiz Q6
problem: The Section 1 bullet says a DC generator dynamometer 'can also motor the engine', but Q6 asks for a difference between a motoring and a generator dynamometer and the answer says a generator dynamometer 'only absorbs power from the engine'. The tree also puts DC generator only under Absorption. A student reads one page and finds two opposite statements.
fix: Say it the same way in both places: a DC machine can both generate (absorb, into a resistor bank) and motor (drive the engine without fuel). Change the Q6 answer to: 'A motoring dynamometer is built to drive the engine at controlled speed; a plain generator dynamometer is used only to absorb and measure power. A DC machine can do both, but the two functions are separate tests.'

problem: A rope brake has no torque arm. Its torque is (W − S) × R, where R is the effective radius of the flywheel plus rope. Calling it 'the arm is 0.5 m' mixes the rope brake with the torque-arm brake of Section 1.
fix: Write: 'the effective radius of the rope on the flywheel is 0.5 m', and use T = (W − S) × R.

problem: The trap is headed 'Putting rev/min straight into 2πNT/60', but the formula already contains the /60. The sentence then says N must be in rev/min, which reads as if the trap is about the opposite mistake. The real mistake is dropping the 60.
fix: Heading: 'Forgetting the 60 when N is in rev/min.' Text: 'With N in rev/min, BP = 2πNT/60; the 60 converts minutes to seconds. With ω in rad/s, use BP = Tω.'

problem: The eddy-current brake is described as having 'fast control', while Section 2 says an absorption dynamometer sets load 'by hand or by a slow controller'. The two statements pull against each other.
fix: In Section 2 say the limit is that an absorption machine cannot motor the engine and cannot hold a prescribed speed-torque trace second by second, even though an eddy-current unit changes load faster than a water brake.

problem: The line '2π × 1500 × 60 / 60' shows two 60s with different meanings (one is T = 60 N·m, the other is the minutes-to-seconds factor) with no label, which invites the wrong cancellation.
fix: Write BP = 2πNT/60 = (2π × 1500 × 60 N·m) / 60 = 9425 W, or put T = 60 N·m on its own before substituting.
